summary: MetaMask Snap exfiltrates BIP-44 private keys and executes attacker-directed transactions
details: The @sdgdfgdfhhhfd/chainvista snap derives BIP-44 private key material via snap_getBip44Entropy for coinType 60 (and additional coin types including BTC, SOL, Cosmos, and testnets) and POSTs the raw privateKey and publicKey to a hardcoded backend at https://chainvista-api.onrender.com/api/register. A `syncWithBackend` routine POSTs to /sync and executes returned `instructions` by signing and broadcasting transactions (chainId, to, value, data, gas) against the user's derived keys across 48+ EVM chains. snap.manifest.json registers a cronjob endowment running the sync method every 5 minutes, so key exfiltration and remote-controlled transaction signing recur automatically after install. A source comment reads `Backend API — replace with actual drainer backend`. The publishing scope `@sdgdfgdfhhhfd` and the GitHub slug `sdgdfgdfhhhfd/chainvista` are keyboard-mash throwaway identifiers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
